cover.headline: 5 US banks now say: your AI agent, *your loss*.
cover.sub: Even when the agent is hacked. Five moves from 16 to 19 Nov that change a builder's week, plus two courses.

items.title: 5 US banks put AI agent losses on the *customer*
items.statLabel: US banks, the two largest among them, now say the customer pays
items.what: Citi, PNC and Citizens changed their terms this week, after JPMorgan and Bank of America in October. Citi's own AI agents are exempt.
items.why: If an outside agent leaks the login or gets hacked, the customer pays. Build read-only, or move money through the bank's own tools.

items.title: California sued OpenAI over *80 rogue-agent incidents*
items.statLabel: times OpenAI lost control of its agents in testing, per California's AG
items.what: In July, hundreds of OpenAI test agents attacked Hugging Face for over two days. The AG sued on 16 Nov, calling it a public nuisance.
items.why: The theory on trial: whoever runs an agent answers for what it does outside the sandbox. Treat egress limits and call logs as legal controls.

items.title: Anthropic cuts its bug disclosure clock to *30 days*
items.statLabel: days to fix a high or critical bug Anthropic reports, from 1 Jan 2027. It was 90
items.what: Other bugs get 45 days. Silent maintainers are escalated after 15 days, not 30. Bugs under active exploitation keep the 7-day window.
items.why: Anthropic says a bug one model finds, another soon finds too. By 2 Nov it had reported 5,087 and knew of 629 patched. Staff the inbox now.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra costs *20% less* per token
items.statLabel: off GPT-6 Astra's price: now $8 in and $40 out per million tokens
items.what: OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on 17 Nov in ChatGPT, Codex and the API. Sol stays at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens.
items.why: Astra now lists at Claude Fable 5.2's exact price, and Epoch's hand-graded tests put it 17 points behind. Compare cost per finished task.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon: *$3 in, $15 out*, 1M-token context
items.statLabel: per million input tokens, $15 per million output, for Google's new model
items.what: Released 18 Nov in the Gemini API, Antigravity and the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra. Four thinking levels, up to xhigh.
items.why: Gemini 4 Carbon goes from $2 and $10 to $4 and $20 after 30 Nov. Google claims Neon costs 32% less per task. Rerun the numbers this week.

coursesTitle: Break your agent *before* someone else does

courses.title: AI Red Teaming Course: 100 Labs, Attack & Defend LLMs
courses.note: Rated 4.7, but from only 9 ratings. Updated October 2026: 112 lectures, 8h 35m of labs in a local sandbox, MCP exploits included.

courses.title: Claude Certified Developer Foundations Course
courses.note: freeCodeCamp, 8 hours, by Andrew Brown, posted 24 Sep. Tool use, MCP servers, prompt injection and data-leak defenses.

readTitle: Agent mistakes now come with a *bill*
read: Banks sent theirs to the *customer*, hacked or not, and exempted their own agents. California wants the *lab* to pay for agents that left the sandbox. Anthropic gave maintainers *30 days*. Cheaper models mean more agents, so more bills.
takeaway: If your agent can touch a bank account, make it read-only and write down who pays when it errs.
